record.original_question: Let A and B be generators of C0 semigroups. Under which condition does C := A2 + B 2 generate an analytic semigroup?

evidence.quote: Problem 4 (Sum of squares). Let A and B be generators of C0 semigroups. Under which condition does C := A2 + B 2 generate an analytic semigroup?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space. Recall that a family $\{T(t)\}_{t\geq 0}$ of bounded linear operators on $X$ is called a strongly continuous (or $C_0$) semigroup if $T(0)=I$, $T(t+s)=T(t)T(s)$ for all $t,s\geq 0$, and $\lim_{t\to 0^+}T(t)x=x$ for every $x\in X$. Its infinitesimal generator is the (in general unbounded) closed densely defined operator $A$ with domain $D(A)=\{x\in X:\lim_{t\to 0^+}t^{-1}(T(t)x-x)\text{ exists}\}$ and $Ax=\lim_{t\to 0^+}t^{-1}(T(t)x-x)$. The semigroup $\{T(t)\}_{t\geq 0}$ is called analytic (or holomorphic) if there is a sector $\Sigma_\theta=\{z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}:|\arg z|<\theta\}$ with $\theta\in(0,\pi/2]$ to which $t\mapsto T(t)$ extends as a holomorphic operator-valued function that is uniformly bounded on every smaller subsector and strongly continuous at $0$.

Suppose $A$ and $B$ are generators of $C_0$ semigroups on $X$. Define the operator
$$C := A^2 + B^2$$
on a suitable common domain (for instance $D(A^2)\cap D(B^2)$, with closure if needed). Determine general necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(A,B)$ under which $C$ (or its closure) is the infinitesimal generator of an analytic semigroup on $X$.
